founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-bara: Ratify 'create' / 'Creator' for all 14 Isaiah sites (overlay bara-create-isaiah). Yes, the Genesis 'shape' should be reviewed at the next Genesis pass. Reasons: (1) the Qal/Niphal never takes an accusative of material and the lexica gloss it 'create' (BDB; HALOT brʾ I; Bernhardt TDOT 2; Schmidt THAT 1). (2) The central bara rationale's 'Piel "cut out, fashion"' is the separate homonym 'cut down, clear (forest)' (Josh 17:15, 18; Ezek 23:47; HALOT). Its '(Gesenius §17)' locator is wrong as a GKC reference, since GKC §17 treats Qere/Ketiv. (3) The central yatsar entry glosses yāṣar 'form, shape, fashion (as a potter)', so 'shape' for bārāʾ already collides with the potter's verb even in Genesis. (4) The canon itself uses 'créés, formés et faits' (Isa 43:7). Corpus finding: AMO-WOH-4:13 already renders bôrēʾ rûaḥ 'shapes the wind', an extension of the Genesis 'shape' outside the central appliesTo that is now inconsistent with Isaiah. Review it together with the Genesis decision. Options for the Genesis review: re-render 'create' and keep the bārāʾ/ʿāśāh/yāṣar distinction as create/make/form (the Isaiah model), or keep 'shape' but downgrade the central entry to speculative with a corrected rationale.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-divine-ruach: Accept the genre-based split: lower-case 'spirit' in Isaiah's endowment/outpouring poetry and 'ruach' in Kings/Ezekiel agent narratives. The weak point is Ezekiel's own endowment/outpouring verses: 37:14 'I will put my ruach in you' is published, and 36:27 and 39:29 are not yet translated in this data. These share Isaiah's sense rather than the 'agent that lifts' sense that justifies transliteration. At the next Ezekiel pass, decide whether those few sites should move to 'my spirit' or stay 'ruach' for in-book consistency. Either way, add reciprocal cross-references 44:3 ↔ Ezek 37:14 now, and to 39:29 once it is translated. Do not transliterate in Isaiah.

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֣את בֵּֽית־יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַנִּקְרָאִים֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִמֵּ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יָצָ֑אוּ הַֽנִּשְׁבָּעִ֣ים ׀ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה וּבֵאלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יַזְכִּ֔ירוּ לֹ֥א בֶאֱמֶ֖ת וְלֹ֥א בִצְדָקָֽה׃

i18n.en: Hear this, O house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel, and who came forth from the waters of Judah; who swear by the name of YHWH and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth nor in righteousness.
i18n.he: שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֣את בֵּֽית־יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַנִּקְרָאִים֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִמֵּ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יָצָ֑אוּ הַֽנִּשְׁבָּעִ֣ים ׀ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה וּבֵאלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יַזְכִּ֔ירוּ לֹ֥א בֶאֱמֶ֖ת וְלֹ֥א בִצְדָקָֽה׃

notes.official: MT *ûmim-mê yᵉhûḏāh yāṣāʾû* is “and who came forth from the waters of Judah” (ASV). The phrase is commonly emended to *ûmim-mᵉʿê* “from the loins (bowels) of Judah” (cf. *mēʿeḵā* “your body,” 48:19; NRSV “from the loins of Judah”), and the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) reads ממעי, which supports the emendation. The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* is “the God of Israel” (overlay construct-epithet pattern).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־מֵעִ֤יר הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ נִקְרָ֔אוּ וְעַל־אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִסְמָ֑כוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For they call themselves after the holy city, and lean upon the God of Israel; YHWH of hosts is his name.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־מֵעִ֤יר הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ נִקְרָ֔אוּ וְעַל־אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִסְמָ֑כוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: הָרִֽאשֹׁנוֹת֙ מֵאָ֣ז הִגַּ֔דְתִּי וּמִפִּ֥י יָצְא֖וּ וְאַשְׁמִיעֵ֑ם פִּתְאֹ֥ם עָשִׂ֖יתִי וַתָּבֹֽאנָה׃

i18n.en: The former things I declared long ago; they went out from my mouth, and I made them heard; suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
i18n.he: הָרִֽאשֹׁנוֹת֙ מֵאָ֣ז הִגַּ֔דְתִּי וּמִפִּ֥י יָצְא֖וּ וְאַשְׁמִיעֵ֑ם פִּתְאֹ֥ם עָשִׂ֖יתִי וַתָּבֹֽאנָה׃

notes.official: *hā-rīšōnôṯ mēʾāz higgaḏtî* “The former things I declared long ago.” The argument from prophecy runs through chs. 41–48: YHWH announced events before they happened, and the idols could not. *ʿāśîṯî* “I acted” is the general verb *ʿāśāh*.

paragraphs.text: מִדַּעְתִּ֕י כִּ֥י קָשֶׁ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וְגִ֤יד בַּרְזֶל֙ עָרְפֶּ֔ךָ וּמִצְחֲךָ֖ נְחוּשָֽׁה׃

i18n.en: Because I knew that you are obstinate, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead bronze,
i18n.he: מִדַּעְתִּ֕י כִּ֥י קָשֶׁ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וְגִ֤יד בַּרְזֶל֙ עָרְפֶּ֔ךָ וּמִצְחֲךָ֖ נְחוּשָֽׁה׃

paragraphs.text: וָאַגִּ֤יד לְךָ֙ מֵאָ֔ז בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֑יךָ פֶּן־תֹּאמַר֙ עָצְבִּ֣י עָשָׂ֔ם וּפִסְלִ֥י וְנִסְכִּ֖י צִוָּֽם׃

i18n.en: I declared it to you long ago; before it came I made you hear it, lest you should say, “My idol did them, and my carved image and my molten image commanded them.”
i18n.he: וָאַגִּ֤יד לְךָ֙ מֵאָ֔ז בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֑יךָ פֶּן־תֹּאמַר֙ עָצְבִּ֣י עָשָׂ֔ם וּפִסְלִ֥י וְנִסְכִּ֖י צִוָּֽם׃

paragraphs.text: שָׁמַ֤עְתָּֽ חֲזֵה֙ כֻּלָּ֔הּ וְאַתֶּ֖ם הֲל֣וֹא תַגִּ֑ידוּ הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֤יךָ חֲדָשׁוֹת֙ מֵעַ֔תָּה וּנְצֻר֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽם׃

i18n.en: You have heard; see all of it! And you — will you not declare it? From now on I make you hear new things, hidden things that you have not known.
i18n.he: שָׁמַ֤עְתָּֽ חֲזֵה֙ כֻּלָּ֔הּ וְאַתֶּ֖ם הֲל֣וֹא תַגִּ֑ידוּ הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֤יךָ חֲדָשׁוֹת֙ מֵעַ֔תָּה וּנְצֻר֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽם׃

paragraphs.text: עַתָּ֤ה נִבְרְאוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מֵאָ֔ז וְלִפְנֵי־י֖וֹם וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתָּ֑ם פֶּן־תֹּאמַ֖ר הִנֵּ֥ה יְדַעְתִּֽין׃

i18n.en: They are created now, and not long ago; before today you had not heard of them, lest you should say, “Behold, I knew them.”
i18n.he: עַתָּ֤ה נִבְרְאוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מֵאָ֔ז וְלִפְנֵי־י֖וֹם וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתָּ֑ם פֶּן־תֹּאמַ֖ר הִנֵּ֥ה יְדַעְתִּֽין׃

notes.official: *ʿattāh niḇrᵉʾû* “They are created now” (Niphal of *bārāʾ*), said of the “new things” of v. 6. That the verb here takes events in history as its object is one reason the Editor renders *bārāʾ* “create” in Isaiah rather than extending the Genesis-scoped central `bara` (“shape”): new events are not shaped from a material (overlay `bara-create-isaiah`; ASV, NRSV, NJPS “created”).

paragraphs.text: גַּ֣ם לֹֽא־שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ גַּ֚ם לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתָּ גַּ֕ם מֵאָ֖ז לֹא־פִתְּחָ֣ה אָזְנֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ בָּג֣וֹד תִּבְגּ֔וֹד וּפֹשֵׁ֥עַ מִבֶּ֖טֶן קֹ֥רָא לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: You have neither heard nor known, nor from of old has your ear been opened; for I knew that you would deal very treacherously, and from the womb you were called a transgressor.
i18n.he: גַּ֣ם לֹֽא־שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ גַּ֚ם לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתָּ גַּ֕ם מֵאָ֖ז לֹא־פִתְּחָ֣ה אָזְנֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ בָּג֣וֹד תִּבְגּ֔וֹד וּפֹשֵׁ֥עַ מִבֶּ֖טֶן קֹ֥רָא לָֽךְ׃

paragraphs.text: לְמַ֤עַן שְׁמִי֙ אַאֲרִ֣יךְ אַפִּ֔י וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י אֶחֱטָם־לָ֑ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הַכְרִיתֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: For my name's sake I defer my anger, and for my praise I restrain it for you, that I may not cut you off.
i18n.he: לְמַ֤עַן שְׁמִי֙ אַאֲרִ֣יךְ אַפִּ֔י וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י אֶחֱטָם־לָ֑ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הַכְרִיתֶֽךָ׃

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֥ה צְרַפְתִּ֖יךָ וְלֹ֣א בְכָ֑סֶף בְּחַרְתִּ֖יךָ בְּכ֥וּר עֹֽנִי׃

i18n.en: Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֥ה צְרַפְתִּ֖יךָ וְלֹ֣א בְכָ֑סֶף בְּחַרְתִּ֖יךָ בְּכ֥וּר עֹֽנִי׃

notes.official:
MT *bᵉḥartîḵā bᵉḵûr ʿōnî* is “I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction” (ASV). The parallel *ṣᵉraptîḵā* “I have refined you” suggests “tested.” That sense is available either from *bḥr* in its Aramaic sense “test” or from the Great Isaiah Scroll’s reading בחנתיכה *bᵉḥantîḵā* “I have tried you” (NRSV and NJPS “tested”). The line keeps MT’s “chosen” and records the alternative (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *lōʾ ḵᵉḵāsep̄* “but not as silver”: the refining was not carried as far as a silversmith would carry it.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes vv. 10–11 (in French « je t’ai éprouvé dans le creuset du malheur », “I tested you,” in English “I have chosen thee”) in a passage on the creators leaving humanity to progress alone. The two wordings match the two readings set out above. The line follows MT.

paragraphs.text: לְמַעֲנִ֧י לְמַעֲנִ֛י אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה כִּ֣י אֵ֣יךְ יֵחָ֑ל וּכְבוֹדִ֖י לְאַחֵ֥ר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּֽן׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For my own sake, for my own sake I do it — for how should it be profaned? — and my glory I will not give to another.
i18n.he: לְמַעֲנִ֧י לְמַעֲנִ֛י אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה כִּ֣י אֵ֣יךְ יֵחָ֑ל וּכְבוֹדִ֖י לְאַחֵ֥ר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּֽן׃ (ס)

notes.official: *lᵉmaʿănî lᵉmaʿănî ʾeʿĕśeh kî ʾêḵ yēḥāl* “For my own sake, for my own sake I do it — for how should it be profaned?” MT’s verb has no expressed subject. ASV and NRSV supply “my name” from v. 9, with the LXX, which reads “for my name is profaned”; the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) reads the first person, “how should I be profaned?” The line keeps the MT construction without supplying a subject (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The canon quotes the verse with v. 10; see the note there.

paragraphs.text: שְׁמַ֤ע אֵלַי֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מְקֹרָאִ֑י אֲנִי־הוּא֙ אֲנִ֣י רִאשׁ֔וֹן אַ֖ף אֲנִ֥י אַחֲרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel, my called one: I am he; I am the first, I am also the last.
i18n.he: שְׁמַ֤ע אֵלַי֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מְקֹרָאִ֑י אֲנִי־הוּא֙ אֲנִ֣י רִאשׁ֔וֹן אַ֖ף אֲנִ֥י אַחֲרֽוֹן׃

paragraphs.text: אַף־יָדִי֙ יָ֣סְדָה אֶ֔רֶץ וִֽימִינִ֖י טִפְּחָ֣ה שָׁמָ֑יִם קֹרֵ֥א אֲנִ֛י אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יַעַמְד֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃

i18n.en: My hand also laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand spread out the skies; when I call to them, they stand up together.
i18n.he: אַף־יָדִי֙ יָ֣סְדָה אֶ֔רֶץ וִֽימִינִ֖י טִפְּחָ֣ה שָׁמָ֑יִם קֹרֵ֥א אֲנִ֛י אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יַעַמְד֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃

notes.official: *yāḏî yāsᵉḏāh ʾereṣ wîmînî ṭippᵉḥāh šāmāyim* “My hand also laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand spread out the skies.” *šāmayim* is in the creation register (“skies”), as at 40:12, 22. *ʾereṣ* is “the earth” in the cosmic pair. *qōrēʾ ʾănî ʾălêhem yaʿamḏû yaḥdāw* “when I call to them, they stand up together,” like servants at attention.

paragraphs.text: הִקָּבְצ֤וּ כֻלְּכֶם֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔עוּ מִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם הִגִּ֣יד אֶת־אֵ֑לֶּה יְהוָ֣ה אֲהֵב֔וֹ יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה חֶפְצוֹ֙ בְּבָבֶ֔ל וּזְרֹע֖וֹ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

i18n.en: Assemble, all of you, and hear! Who among them has declared these things? He whom YHWH loves shall do his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans.
i18n.he: הִקָּבְצ֤וּ כֻלְּכֶם֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔עוּ מִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם הִגִּ֣יד אֶת־אֵ֑לֶּה יְהוָ֣ה אֲהֵב֔וֹ יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה חֶפְצוֹ֙ בְּבָבֶ֔ל וּזְרֹע֖וֹ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

paragraphs.text: אֲנִ֥י אֲנִ֛י דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אַף־קְרָאתִ֑יו הֲבִיאֹתִ֖יו וְהִצְלִ֥יחַ דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: I, I have spoken; yes, I have called him; I have brought him, and his way shall prosper.
i18n.he: אֲנִ֥י אֲנִ֛י דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אַף־קְרָאתִ֑יו הֲבִיאֹתִ֖יו וְהִצְלִ֥יחַ דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃

paragraphs.text: קִרְב֧וּ אֵלַ֣י שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֗את לֹ֤א מֵרֹאשׁ֙ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי מֵעֵ֥ת הֱיוֹתָ֖הּ שָׁ֣ם אָ֑נִי וְעַתָּ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה שְׁלָחַ֖נִי וְרוּחֽוֹ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Draw near to me, hear this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it came to be, I was there. And now the Lord YHWH has sent me, and his spirit.
i18n.he: קִרְב֧וּ אֵלַ֣י שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֗את לֹ֤א מֵרֹאשׁ֙ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי מֵעֵ֥ת הֱיוֹתָ֖הּ שָׁ֣ם אָ֑נִי וְעַתָּ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה שְׁלָחַ֖נִי וְרוּחֽוֹ׃ (פ)

notes.official: *wᵉʿattāh ʾăḏōnāy YHWH šᵉlāḥanî wᵉrûḥô* “And now the Lord YHWH has sent me, and his spirit.” Two ambiguities are left open as the Hebrew leaves them. (1) *rûḥô* may be a second object (“has sent me and his spirit,” ASV) or a second subject (“the Lord YHWH and his spirit have sent me,” KJV tradition). (2) The speaker who suddenly says “me” is not identified: the prophet, the servant, or Cyrus have all been proposed. *rûḥô* is lower-case “his spirit” (overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah`). *ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* is “the Lord YHWH” (overlay compound-name entry).

paragraphs.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְךָ֖ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ מְלַמֶּדְךָ֣ לְהוֹעִ֔יל מַדְרִֽיכֲךָ֖ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ תֵּלֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: Thus says YHWH, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am YHWH your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you in the way you should go.
i18n.he: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְךָ֖ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ מְלַמֶּדְךָ֣ לְהוֹעִ֔יל מַדְרִֽיכֲךָ֖ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ תֵּלֵֽךְ׃

paragraphs.text: ל֥וּא הִקְשַׁ֖בְתָּ לְמִצְוֺתָ֑י וַיְהִ֤י כַנָּהָר֙ שְׁלוֹמֶ֔ךָ וְצִדְקָתְךָ֖ כְּגַלֵּ֥י הַיָּֽם׃

i18n.en: O that you had paid attention to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea;
i18n.he: ל֥וּא הִקְשַׁ֖בְתָּ לְמִצְוֺתָ֑י וַיְהִ֤י כַנָּהָר֙ שְׁלוֹמֶ֔ךָ וְצִדְקָתְךָ֖ כְּגַלֵּ֥י הַיָּֽם׃

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י כַחוֹל֙ זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וְצֶאֱצָאֵ֥י מֵעֶ֖יךָ כִּמְעֹתָ֑יו לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת וְֽלֹא־יִשָּׁמֵ֛ד שְׁמ֖וֹ מִלְּפָנָֽי׃

i18n.en: your seed would have been like the sand, and the offspring of your body like its grains; his name would not be cut off nor destroyed from before me.
i18n.he: וַיְהִ֤י כַחוֹל֙ זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וְצֶאֱצָאֵ֥י מֵעֶ֖יךָ כִּמְעֹתָ֑יו לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת וְֽלֹא־יִשָּׁמֵ֛ד שְׁמ֖וֹ מִלְּפָנָֽי׃

paragraphs.text: צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ בִּרְח֣וּ מִכַּשְׂדִּים֒ בְּק֣וֹל רִנָּ֗ה הַגִּ֤ידוּ הַשְׁמִ֙יעוּ֙ זֹ֔את הוֹצִיא֖וּהָ עַד־קְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ אִמְר֕וּ גָּאַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה עַבְדּ֥וֹ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans! With a voice of singing declare this, proclaim it, send it out to the end of the earth; say: “YHWH has redeemed his servant Jacob.”
i18n.he: צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ בִּרְח֣וּ מִכַּשְׂדִּים֒ בְּק֣וֹל רִנָּ֗ה הַגִּ֤ידוּ הַשְׁמִ֙יעוּ֙ זֹ֔את הוֹצִיא֖וּהָ עַד־קְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ אִמְר֕וּ גָּאַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה עַבְדּ֥וֹ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

notes.official: *gāʾal YHWH ʿaḇdô yaʿăqōḇ* “YHWH has redeemed his servant Jacob.” The servant here is Jacob/Israel by name (overlay `eved-servant-identity-isaiah`). The call to leave Babylon presents the return as a new exodus, and v. 21 recalls the water from the rock (Exod 17:6; Num 20:11).

paragraphs.text: וְלֹ֣א צָמְא֗וּ בָּחֳרָבוֹת֙ הֽוֹלִיכָ֔ם מַ֥יִם מִצּ֖וּר הִזִּ֣יל לָ֑מוֹ וַיִּ֨בְקַע־צ֔וּר וַיָּזֻ֖בוּ מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And they did not thirst when he led them through the deserts; he made water flow from the rock for them; he split the rock, and the water gushed out.
i18n.he: וְלֹ֣א צָמְא֗וּ בָּחֳרָבוֹת֙ הֽוֹלִיכָ֔ם מַ֥יִם מִצּ֖וּר הִזִּ֣יל לָ֑מוֹ וַיִּ֨בְקַע־צ֔וּר וַיָּזֻ֖בוּ מָֽיִם׃

paragraphs.text: אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים׃ (ס)

i18n.en: There is no peace, says YHWH, for the wicked.
i18n.he: אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים׃ (ס)
